source_text: Qui fidem resurrectionis ante istos Sadducaeorum propinquos sine controversia moratam ita student inquietare, ut eam spem negent etiam ad carnem pertinere, merito Christi quoque carnem quaestionibus distrahunt, tamquam aut nullam omnino aut quoquo modo aliam praeter humanam, ne, si humanam constiterit fuisse, praeiudicatum sit adversus illos eam resurgere omni modo, quae in Christo resurrexerit. Igitur unde illi destruunt carnis vota, inde nobis erunt praestruenda. Examinemus corporalem substantiam domini; de spiritali enim certum est. Caro quaeritur. Veritas et qualitas eius retractatur: an fuerit, et unde, et cuiusmodi fuerit. Renuntiatio eius dabit legem nostrae resurrectioni. Marcion, ut carnem Christi negaret, negavit etiam nativitatem, aut ut nativitatem negaret, negavit et carnem, scilicet ne invicem sibi testimonium responderent nativitas et caro, quia nec nativitas sine carne nec caro sine nativitate; quasi non eadem licentia haeretica et ipse potuisset aut admissa carne nativitatem negare, ut Apelles discipulus et postea desertor ipsius, aut et carnem et nativitatem confessus aliter illas interpretari, ut condiscipulus et condesertor eius Valentinus. Sed et qui carnem Christi putativam introduxit, aeque potuit nativitatem quoque phantasma confingere, ut et conceptus et praegnatus et partus virginis et ipsius exinde infantis ordo τῷ δοκεῖν haberentur. Eosdem oculos eosdemque sensus fefellissent quos carnis opinio elusit.
thought_title: The resurrection of the flesh depends on Christ's true flesh
orientation: Tertullian opens his treatise by stating that those who deny the resurrection of the flesh also attack the reality of Christ's flesh, and he will now examine the bodily substance of the Lord.
pass_a_gloss: Those who, before these Sadducees' relatives, strive to disturb the faith of the resurrection which has remained without controversy, so that they deny that this hope pertains also to the flesh, deservedly tear apart also the flesh of Christ with questions, as if it were either none at all or in some way other than human, lest, if it should be established that it was human, it be prejudged against them that that flesh rises in every way, which rose in Christ. Therefore from where they destroy the desires of the flesh, from there the defenses must be built up for us. Let us examine the bodily substance of the Lord; for about the spiritual one it is certain. The flesh is in question. Its truth and quality is reconsidered: whether it existed, and from where, and of what sort it was. The report of it will give the law to our resurrection. Marcion, in order to deny the flesh of Christ, denied also the birth, or in order to deny the birth, denied also the flesh, evidently so that birth and flesh would not answer as testimony to each other, because neither birth without flesh nor flesh without birth; as if with the same heretical license he himself could not have either, with the flesh admitted, denied the birth, as Apelles, his disciple and later deserter, or, having confessed both flesh and birth, interpreted them otherwise, as his fellow disciple and fellow deserter Valentinus. But also he who introduced the flesh of Christ as supposed could equally have fabricated the birth also as a phantom, so that both the conception and the pregnancy and the delivery of the virgin and the subsequent order of the infant would be held by seeming. The same eyes and the same senses would have been deceived which the opinion of the flesh eluded.

lemmas.gloss: tear apart, pull in different directions
to be built up beforehand, prepared

choices.why: Vota here means the hopes or desires directed toward the flesh, i.e., the resurrection hopes for the flesh; kept literal to preserve the possessive force.

choices.english: the defenses must be built up
choices.why: Praestruere means to build up beforehand or prepare defenses; the passive periphrastic conveys necessity, matching the argumentative structure.

choices.english: the bodily substance of the Lord
choices.why: Substantia is a fixed glossary term rendered as substance; corporalis is rendered bodily to keep the adjective-noun structure.
rejected: the corporeal substance of the Lord

choices.why: Putativus means supposed or imaginary; rendered as supposed to preserve the technical sense of a body that only seems to exist.
The Greek dative phrase means in appearance or by seeming; kept as a literal rendering of the Greek idiom Tertullian uses.

pass_b_english: Those who want to unsettle the faith in the resurrection—which before these near relatives of the Sadducees remained without controversy—by denying that this hope extends to the flesh, quite logically tear apart the flesh of Christ with their questions. They claim it was either nothing at all or somehow other than human, because if it is established that it was human, the case is already decided against them: whatever rose in Christ must rise in every way. So the very point from which they destroy the claims of the flesh is where the defenses must be built up for us. Let us examine the bodily substance of the Lord; about the spiritual substance there is no dispute. The flesh is what is in question. Its truth and its quality are being reconsidered: whether it existed, and from where, and of what kind it was. The report of it will give the law for our resurrection. Marcion, in order to deny the flesh of Christ, denied also his birth—or in order to deny his birth, denied his flesh. Naturally, he did not want birth and flesh to testify for each other, since there is no birth without flesh and no flesh without birth. As if he himself could not, with the same heretical license, have either admitted the flesh and denied the birth, as Apelles did—his disciple and later his deserter—or confessed both the flesh and the birth and interpreted them differently, as Valentinus did, his fellow disciple and fellow deserter. But even the man who introduced a supposed flesh of Christ could equally have fabricated the birth as a phantom, so that the conception, the pregnancy, the delivery of the virgin, and the whole course of the infant's life from then on would be held by seeming. They would have deceived the same eyes and the same senses that the supposition of flesh deceived.

problems.why: vota here means vows/claims/pledges, not desires; this is about the case for the flesh, not carnal desires.
problems.ruling: "carnis vota" means vows/claims about the flesh, not flesh's desires; translation changes meaning.

fixed: Changed 'the desires of the flesh' to 'the claims of the flesh' because 'vota' here means vows/claims/pledges, not desires.

problems.quote: The same eyes and the same senses would have been deceived that the opinion of flesh eluded.
problems.source_quote: Eosdem oculos eosdemque sensus fefellissent quos carnis opinio elusit.
problems.why: Those appearances would have deceived the same eyes and senses that the supposition of flesh deceived. Elusit means deceived, and the relative clause is broken.
problems.fix: They would have deceived the same eyes and the same senses which the supposition of flesh deceived.
problems.ruling: 'quos carnis opinio elusit': the supposition of flesh deceived those eyes. 'Eluded' reverses the sense, and 'would have been deceived that...' is broken.

edits.old: The same eyes and the same senses would have been deceived that the opinion of flesh eluded.
edits.new: They would have deceived the same eyes and the same senses that the supposition of flesh deceived.

fixed: Fixed voice and verb: fefellissent is active and elusit means deceived, so the phantom birth events would have deceived the same eyes/senses the supposition of flesh deceived.

last_rejected.quote: because if it is established that it was human, the case is already decided against them: whatever rose in Christ must rise in every way
last_rejected.source_quote: ne, si humanam constiterit fuisse, praeiudicatum sit adversus illos eam resurgere omni modo, quae in Christo resurrexerit
last_rejected.why: Purpose (lest) becomes cause, and the prejudgment is that the flesh which rose in Christ rises wholly, not that whatever rose must rise.
last_rejected.fix: lest, if it is established that it was human, it be already decided against them that the flesh which rose in Christ rises in every way
last_rejected.ruling: "ne… praeiudicatum sit" is rendered as a reason ("because… already decided against them"). The sense of avoiding prejudgment is kept, and "eam… quae in Christo resurrexerit" is conveyed. It is a stylistic nuance, not a meaning change.
